title: What are the array declaration and initialization forms in Java?
shortTitle: What are the array declaration and initialization forms in Java?
keyPoints: Arrays are fixed-size, type-safe containers stored contiguously on the heap
Declaration: int[] arr; or int arr[]; (prefer int[] style)
Creation: new int[5] allocates with default values (0/null/false)
Initialization: int[] arr = {10, 20, 30}; or new int[]{10, 20, 30}
Length is fixed at creation – cannot grow or shrink – use ArrayList for dynamic sizing
Array index starts at 0, accessing out of bounds throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException

s1_definition.oneliner: An array is a fixed-size, indexed container of elements of the same type. Declare with int[], create with new int[n], initialize with {values}.
s1_definition.profdef:
Array basics:

- **Fixed size.** Set at creation, cannot change.
- **Type-safe.** int[] holds only ints. String[] holds only Strings.
- **Zero-indexed.** First element at index 0, last at length-1.
- **Heap-allocated.** The array object lives on the heap. Elements are stored contiguously.
s1_definition.analogy: An array is a row of fixed-size bank lockers. You choose how many lockers when you build the row. Each locker is numbered starting from 0. You can put one item in each locker, and accessing a locker number that does not exist is an error.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Arrays are fixed-size, type-safe containers stored contiguously on the heap. Declare with `int[]`, create with `new int[n]`, and initialize with `{values}`. Elements default to 0, false, or null. Accessing out of bounds throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

For dynamic sizing, use ArrayList. For fixed-size performance-critical code, use arrays.

One sentence to remember: arrays are fixed-size, zero-indexed, heap-allocated – use ArrayList when you need dynamic sizing.
